description: VERDICT: KILLED. Issue #843: DCExtension.ApplyDataPrivilegeForAnalysis used to fail OPEN whenever WTMContext.LoginUserInfo == null -- it returned the caller's query completely unfiltered instead of denying it. Every background execution path (DashboardSnapshotJob, DashboardAlertHostedService) resolves WTMContext from a bare IServiceProvider.CreateScope() with no HttpContext, so LoginUserInfo is always null there -- row-level DataPrivilege was silently skipped for every widget those jobs execute. Fixed by making the null-identity path fail CLOSED by default (reusing AppendSelfDPWhere's existing dps==null => '1 != 1' denial for any model with a configured DataPrivilege rule), with a new declaredSystemQuery parameter (default false) as the one explicit, review-visible escape hatch back to the old unfiltered behaviour. This mutant deletes the '&& declaredSystemQuery' conjunct from the guard `if (wtmcontext.LoginUserInfo == null && declaredSystemQuery)`, restoring the exact pre-#843 unconditional fail-open branch -- the production line whose deletion turns the red assertion red.
target_symbol: DCExtension.ApplyDataPrivilegeForAnalysis(IQueryable, WTMContext?, bool) -- the '&& declaredSystemQuery' conjunct on the LoginUserInfo==null guard
red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first) with the mutant patch applied: "Assert.AreEqual failed. Expected:<0>. Actual:<1>. #843: no identity + a DataPrivilege rule configured for this model must deny all rows by default." -- i.e. the query reverts to the exact pre-#843 unfiltered result (the single seeded row is returned instead of being denied).
